attack_mechanism: Corrupting `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_dadd0` during target calculation changes one or more bits of the value presented to the software-PC input. For computed control transfers, the ALU and register-file datapaths produce `reg_dest_val_in`, which becomes `pc_sw` when R0 is the destination or a CALL requests a PC write. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_dadd0` contributes data or a selector to this computed target; the implementation qualifies this propagation with `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.inst_alu`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. The relevant internal route is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_dadd0 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_out_nxt -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest_val_in -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. At the following PC write, execution is redirected to an unintended aligned or misaligned address.

A transient bit flip or forced value on `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_alu_nxt` before the next `mclk` edge can substitute a false target or assert the software-write selection on the wrong instruction. During a CALL, jump, or instruction that writes R0, `pc_sw_wr` has priority in the `pc_nxt` multiplexer and selects `pc_sw`. `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_alu_nxt` participates in forming or qualifying that software-PC path; the implementation qualifies this propagation with `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr`. The relevant internal route is `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_alu_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_alu -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.reg_dest_wr -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. The corrupted target is captured in `pc`, redirecting control flow, skipping intended instructions, or executing an unintended basic block.
